note: Gadgets section, 14-day window (window_hours() returns the design default 72, so 336 is set explicitly per run notes; every item was gated with `python3 pipeline/freshness.py <published_iso> 2026-08-13T22:00:26Z gadgets` and printed FRESH). Published times were read from each article's og article:published_time / JSON-LD datePublished via WebFetch; where the outlet's article body is truncated to our fetcher (techradar.com, tomsguide.com), the time comes from that outlet's own RSS <pubDate> for the same URL (techradar tag feeds artificial-intelligence / smart-glasses / robots; tomsguide feeds/tag/ai). Tom's Guide Pixel 11 Pro Fold has a date-only stamp in the feed, so clock time is approximated to midday and flagged here. Swept allowed_domains: engadget.com, 9to5google.com, 9to5mac.com, macrumors.com, androidauthority.com, gizmodo.com, techradar.com, tomsguide.com, xda-developers.com, tomshardware.com, notebookcheck.net, uploadvr.com, roadtovr.com, venturebeat.com, digitaltrends.com (feeds all returned empty to our fetcher, so no DT items survived). theverge.com, wired.com, cnet.com, arstechnica.com, zdnet.com and reuters.com are blocked to our user agent and could not be searched. Keyword expansion beyond keywords_gadgets.json was needed: 'Made by Google 2026', 'Tensor G6 TPU', 'Pixel Watch 5 / Google Health AI', 'Honor Robot Phone', 'Matic Cues robot vacuum', 'Viture Pro 2', 'Meta Ray-Ban Scriber Optics', 'budget Ray-Ban alternatives', 'Gemini for Home AI Storytime', 'iOS 27 public beta Siri AI'. Dropped for staleness: Plaud agent wearable (Jun 17), UploadVR Meta glasses update (Apr 3), XDA AMD Ryzen AI Halo (May 20), Engadget Notepad local AI (Sep 2025), Engadget Sweekar AI pocket pet (Jan 4), Tom's Guide 'smart glasses ruin wearable displays' (Jul 30 12:00Z, just outside window). Dropped for relevance/duplication: Qualcomm Snapdragon C (no AI/NPU hook), MacRumors Siri publisher-payment talks (business deal, no device hook), TechRadar EU smart-glasses regulation, Gizmodo OpenAI puck speaker (already covered per skip_topics_recent), Apple Houston manufacturing centre, TechRadar Honor Robot Phone hands-on (same story as the Engadget launch item kept below).

items.title: Meta is giving away 15,000 AI glasses to blind and visually impaired people in Ireland
items.excerpt: Meta is handing 15,000 Ray-Ban Meta glasses to charity Vision Ireland, positioning the camera-and-voice wearable as an accessibility device that reads text aloud and describes objects. It is the clearest test yet of whether AI glasses earn their keep as an assistive interface rather than a novelty.

items.title: Honor launches its long-awaited Robot Phone and yes it can wiggle at you
items.excerpt: Honor's Robot Phone ships with a motorised pop-up camera gimbal that rotates 360 degrees and a 'YOYO Robot Mode' that gesture-controls and tracks subjects on its own. It is a rare attempt to give an AI assistant an actual moving body inside a phone.

items.title: Pixel Buds Pro 2 and 2a are getting some upgrades, including deeper Gemini integration
items.excerpt: Google is pushing dynamic noise cancellation and deeper Gemini control to existing Pixel Buds in September, letting the assistant change volume and EQ on command. Existing hardware gets a new interaction model without a new purchase.

items.title: Pixel 11 Pro launches with the best of Google's Gemini Intelligence starting at $1,099 [Hands-on]
items.excerpt: The Pixel 11 Pro pairs the Tensor G6 with Google's fullest Gemini Intelligence stack, adding agentic on-device tasks and a 'HiLight' notification LED, at $1,099. Hands-on impressions frame the phone as an AI-experience release rather than a spec bump.

items.title: Pixel 11 debuts Gboard Rambler, location-aware At a Glance, and more Gemini Intelligence
items.excerpt: Pixel 11 introduces Gboard Rambler, which turns rambling dictation into clean prompted text, plus location-aware At a Glance and proactive suggestions across messaging and productivity apps. Real-time translation also extends to podcasts and video.

items.title: The Pixel Watch 5 isn't much at a glance, until you get to 'At a Glance' [Hands-on]
items.excerpt: Pixel Watch 5 keeps last year's shell but rebuilds the glanceable layer, surfacing timers, navigation and live activity through a redesigned Gemini-fed 'At a Glance' surface. The interesting upgrade is an interface pattern, not the hardware.

items.title: The Tensor G6's new TPU is secretly the best Pixel 11 upgrade no one's talking about
items.excerpt: The Tensor G6's TPU brings 50% more compute and runs local workloads up to 3.5x faster at 3.5x lower energy, letting Gemini Nano handle transcription, sign-to-text and live translation entirely on device. On-device inference, not raw CPU, is where the Pixel 11 actually moved.

items.title: Google Home kicks off August with big app updates and a smarter Gemini for Home
items.excerpt: Gemini for Home adds an interactive AI Storytime mode families can steer by voice, alongside better natural-language handling of alarms and timers and wider third-party camera support. The smart speaker is quietly turning into a conversational content device.

items.title: Matic's Robot Vacuum Will See (and Hear) You Now
items.excerpt: Matic's new 'Matic Cues' firmware adds a 'Hey Matic' wake phrase and gesture control, with Google Gemini parsing compound commands like 'vacuum the dining room rug and then mop the bedroom.' It is a voice-first rewrite of how you operate a home robot.

items.title: Viture Pro 2 Review: A Dark Horse in the Entry-Level AR Glasses Race
items.excerpt: At $299 the Viture Pro 2 delivers a bright micro-OLED wearable display that out-sharpens Xreal and RayNeo rivals, though the companion app is buggy and iPhone users need a dongle. Entry-level wearable displays are getting good enough to be a real second screen.

items.title: 30 New Things Your iPhone Can Do in iOS 27
items.excerpt: MacRumors catalogues 30 shipping iOS 27 changes built around the rebuilt Siri AI, including Apple Intelligence wallpaper extension that generates image content beyond a photo's edges and Safari auto-grouping tabs by topic. A concrete map of where generative AI now sits inside the phone UI.

items.title: iOS 27 public beta 3 is here with Siri AI, iPhone speed upgrades, and more
items.excerpt: Apple's third iOS 27 public beta opens the redesigned, generative Siri AI to non-developers alongside performance work and overhauled parental controls. It is the widest hands-on look yet at Apple's on-device assistant before the September release.

items.title: 'Nonstop lies from the AI': as Google launches the Pixel Watch 5, its redesigned Google Health app is leaving Fitbit users incensed at its crazy hallucinations
items.excerpt: The Pixel Watch 5 arrives just as the redesigned Google Health app's AI coach is hallucinating workouts and stats, and long-time Fitbit users are revolting. A sharp case study in what happens when a generative layer is bolted onto a trusted health interface.

items.title: After three weeks wearing the Meta Ray-Ban Scriber Optics I couldn't be more in love — I just wish smart glasses weren't so controversial
items.excerpt: A three-week long-term wear test of Meta's Scriber Optics AI glasses, weighing daily usefulness against the social backlash that follows camera-equipped eyewear. Useful signal on whether AI glasses survive contact with real life.

items.title: I tried the Pixel 11 Pro Fold and it's more 'Ultra' than Samsung's foldable for $200 less
items.excerpt: Hands-on with the $1,899 Pixel 11 Pro Fold: a 3,600-nit 8-inch inner display, Tensor G6, 5x zoom and AI features including Magic Capture and Gemini proactive suggestions. Google is using the big canvas to sell AI features rather than raw specs.
